headline: Continued the 11 Cross Street multifamily development and stormwater permit to October 15, and approved a 3-2 public comment policy.
summary: Reissued the Order of Conditions for the 397 Transmission Line and ratified an emergency certification for a DPW beaver dam breach at 296 Hampshire Road. Approved up to $400 for moving records and about $193 for rabies testing. Three enforcement cases were lifted, and most others were continued.
decisions: Continued the Notice of Resource Area Delineation for 1-27 Independence Drive to October 15, 2026. Vote unanimous.
Continued the Notice of Intent for the multifamily development at 11 Cross Street to October 15, 2026. Vote unanimous.
Continued the stormwater permit application for 11 Cross Street to October 15, 2026. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #25-016 at 46 Ayer Street to May 20, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #26-008 at 28 West Street to May 20, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #26-007 at 8 Grandview Road to July 1, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #25-008 at 824 Riverside Drive to July 1, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #23-014 at 40 Atkinson Street, Lot 1 to December 3, 2026. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #25-014 at 134 Meriline Avenue to June 17, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #26-003 at 30 Hidden Road to July 15, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Continued Enforcement Order #24-007 at 15 Gleason Street to July 15, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #26-001 at 1 Riverdale Street to July 15, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Lifted the Notice of Violation and Enforcement Order at 39 Tyler Street. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #24-005 at 5 Riverview Circle to May 6, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #23-013 at 52 Linwood Avenue to October 15, 2026. Vote unanimous.
Lifted the Notice of Violation and Enforcement Order at 2 Hayes Street. Vote unanimous.
Lifted the Notice of Violation and Enforcement Order at 484 Broadway. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #25-006 at 15 Ayers Village Road to June 17, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Continued Enforcement Order #25-006 at 2 Muirfield Lane to June 17, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #26-002 at 2 Indian Summer Street to August 19, 2027. Vote unanimous.
Continued Notice of Violation #26-006 at 143B Tyler Street to November 19, 2026. Vote unanimous.
Adopted a policy on public hearings, public meetings, and a three-minute limit for public comment. Vote 3-2.
Ratified the emergency certification for the DPW beaver dam breach at 296 Hampshire Road. Vote unanimous.
Released Commission funds of approximately $193.00 to pay for animal testing after a rabies exposure. Vote unanimous.
Released funds not to exceed $400.00 for a rental truck to move Conservation records. Vote unanimous.
Approved sending a letter to the City Solicitor about the Liam’s Lane tree removal. Vote unanimous.
Reissued the Order of Conditions for the 397 Transmission Line. Vote unanimous.

plain_text:
CITY OF METHUEN 
CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
 
Minutes of a Meeting – October 1, 2026 
The City of Methuen Conservation Commission held public hearings and a public meeting on 
October 1, 2026, at the Searles Building, 41 Pleasant Street, Second Floor Conference Room, 
and via Zoom Web Meeting.  
 
ROLL CALL: 
Present were Dave Di Zazzo, Chair; Kenneth Sateriale, Secretary; Sandra Boulay, 
Commissioner; Rachel Lecher, Commissioner; and Patrice Friant, Commissioner.  A quorum 
was present.  Also present were Chris Parsons, Conservation Officer, and Michelle Davidson, 
Conservation Clerk.  Commissioner Cara Seaman was absent.  
PUBLIC HEARING 
 
1. NOTICES OF INTENT 
A.  Abbreviated Notice of Resource Area Delineation – DEP File #219-1326 – 1-27 
Independence Drive – SRH Colonial Village LLC 
The applicant requested that the matter be continued to October 15, 2026, pending completion of 
the peer review. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to October 15, 2026.  
Seconded by Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
2. CONTINUED NOTICES OF INTENT 
A.  Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1320, MCC File #26-001 – 11 Cross Street – CROSSLD 
QOZB, LLC – Dresser, Williams & Way, Inc. 
(Continued from July 16, 2026) 
 
Steve Dresser of Dresser, Williams & Way, Inc. appeared on behalf of CROSSLD QOZB, LLC 
for the continued public hearing for the multifamily development project.  
Mr.  Dresser reported that the applicant had revised the project following the Commission’s prior 
decision not to allow encroachment and restoration within the 50-foot to 35-foot buffer zone.
Page 2 
The revised design eliminated the four-bay swale detention basin and added a constructed 
wetland in place of that system.  
The applicant submitted responses and revised plans, including pipe velocities, groundwater 
mounding data, and revised Hydro CAD calculations.  Mr.  Dresser stated that the project 
remains a redevelopment project and that stormwater standards had been addressed to the 
maximum extent practicable.  
Mr.  Dresser explained that the stormwater outfall for the constructed wetland is located within 
the 50-foot to 35-foot buffer zone and stated that an outfall from a stormwater management 
facility is specifically allowed in that area.  He stated that the proposed work in that zone is 
limited and extends to approximately 38 feet from the wetland resource area.  
Maria Johnsenberg of Tighe & Bond stated that the peer review was underway and that an 
updated proposal cost had been sent shortly before the meeting.  No Commissioner questions 
were raised.  
The Commission requested that the peer review be completed and reviewed before closing the 
hearing.  The applicant requested continuation to October 15, 2026.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to October 15, 2026.  Seconded 
by Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
PUBLIC MEETING 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER 
The public meeting was called to order at 7:10 PM. 
2. ACCEPTANCE OF AGENDA / AMENDMENTS 
The agenda was amended to add Item U under Old Business and Item A under Other 
Business.  
MOTION: Motion made by Kenneth Sateriale to accept the agenda as amended. Seconded by 
Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
3. ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES – September 3, 2026 and September 10, 2026 
MOTION: Motion made by Kenneth Sateriale to accept the minutes of September 3, 2026 and 
September 10, 2026. Seconded by Patrice Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
4. NEW BUSINESS 
No new business was presented.  
5. OLD BUSINESS 
A.  Stormwater Permit Application – 11 Cross Street – CROSSLD QOZB, LLC – Dresser, 
Williams & Way, Inc. 
(Continued from July 16, 2026) 
 
The Commission continued the stormwater permit application to October 15, 2026, the same 
date as the related Notice of Intent. 
 
MOTION: Motion by Kenneth Sateriale made to continue the matter to October 15, 2026.  
Seconded by Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.
Page 3 
B.  Notice of Violation #25-016 – 46 Ayer Street – Ahsan Saysourivong 
(Continued from August 6, 2026 for marker installation) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the site is in compliance and that markers and posts are 
installed.  The Conservation Officer recommended continuation to late spring.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to May 20, 2027.  Seconded 
by Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
C.  Notice of Violation #26-008 – 28 West Street – Harjinder Singh 
(Continued from August 6, 2026) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the fill had been cleaned of debris.  The applicant was 
instructed to notify the Conservation Office 48 hours before additional fill is brought to the site 
so that the material can be inspected.  The applicant signed paperwork acknowledging the clean-
fill requirements.  Erosion controls had been installed as of September 24, 2026, and an RDA 
had been issued.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to May 20, 2027.  Seconded 
by Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
D.  Notice of Violation #26-007 – 8 Grandview Road – William Kannan 
(Continued from August 6, 2026) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the site is revegetating and that the conservation markers 
and posts are installed.  Continuation to mid-summer was recommended.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to July 1, 2027. Seconded by 
Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
E.  Notice of Violation #25-008 – 824 Riverside Drive – David Turmel 
(Continued from July 16, 2026) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported on site conditions and recommended continuation to early 
summer.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to July 1, 2027.  Seconded by 
Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
F.  Notice of Violation #23-014 – 40 Atkinson Street, Lot 1 – Erica and Kevin Ring 
(Continued from June 18, 2026) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the site has been in compliance for a while and that the 
remaining item is receipt of the as-built plan. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to December 3, 2026.  
Seconded by Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
G.  Notice of Violation #25-014 – 134 Meriline Avenue – C & A Enterprises, LLC 
(Continued from June 18, 2026)
Page 4 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the site is in compliance and that the fence associated 
with the violation had been removed from the premises.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to June 17, 2027. Seconded by 
Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
H.  Notice of Violation #26-003 – 30 Hidden Road – Sam Higginbottom 
(Continued from June 18, 2026) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the site is revegetating and that markers and posts are 
installed.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to July 15, 2027. Seconded.  
All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
I.  Enforcement Order #24-007 – 15 Gleason Street 
(Continued from June 18, 2026 to reassess vegetation growth and ensure that Conservation 
markers have remained undisturbed) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the site is in compliance and recommended continuing 
the matter to mid-summer to check vegetation and confirm that the markers remain undisturbed.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to July 15, 2027.  Seconded by 
Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
J.  Notice of Violation #26-001 – 1 Riverdale Street – Ladistone Coelho 
(Continued from April 2, 2026; moved from the September 17, 2026 canceled meeting) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that there had been no activity in the riverfront area and that 
the area had grown back. 23 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to July 15, 2027.  Seconded by 
Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
K.  Notice of Violation #25-002 / Enforcement Order #25-005 – 39 Tyler Street – Wanderson 
Pimentel (Continued from May 21, 2026; moved from the September 17, 2026 canceled 
meeting) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the site is in compliance and that the site had completed 
two growing seasons.  The Conservation Officer recommended lifting both the Notice of 
Violation and the Enforcement Order.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to lift both the Notice of Violation and the 
Enforcement Order.  Seconded by Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
L.  Notice of Violation #24-005 – 5 Riverview Circle – Barry Thornton 
(Continued from June 4, 2026 to monitor revegetation of resource area; moved from the 
September 17, 2026 canceled meeting)
Page 5 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that a site inspection had not yet been completed.  The 
homeowner had requested that police be present if the Conservation Officer visited the site, and 
coordination had been difficult.  
The Commission discussed that the homeowner could submit documentation to the Conservation 
Office for the file.  The Chair stated that the Commission could not take public input during that 
portion of the public meeting but encouraged the homeowner to submit materials to the office.  
The matter was continued to allow coordination and review during the next growing season. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to May 6, 2027. Seconded by 
Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
 M.  Notice of Violation #23-013 – DEP File #219-873, MCC File #03-029 – 52 Linwood 
Avenue – Ana Diaz (Continued from June 4, 2026 for marker installation/revegetation check; 
moved from the September 17, 2026 canceled meeting) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that all markers are installed, but that the entire area was 
being mowed again.  The Conservation Officer requested additional time to contact the property 
owner. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to October 15, 2026. Seconded 
by Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
N.  Notice of Violation #25-001 / Enforcement Order #25-003 – 2 Hayes Street – Donna Zappala 
(Continued from June 18, 2025; moved from the September 17, 2026 canceled meeting) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the site is in compliance and recommended lifting both 
the Notice of Violation and the Enforcement Order. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to lift both the Notice of Violation and the 
Enforcement Order.  Seconded by Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
O.  Notice of Violation #24-013 / Enforcement Order #24-008 – 484 Broadway – Diarbakerly 
(Continued from October 2, 2025 to assess revegetation) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the site is in compliance and that the area has been 
growing for two years.  The Conservation Officer recommended lifting both the Notice of 
Violation and the Enforcement Order. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to lift both the Notice of Violation and the 
Enforcement Order.  Seconded by Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
P.  Notice of Violation #25-006 / Enforcement Order #25-004 – 15 Ayers Village Road – Elicer 
Gomez (Continued from June 18, 2026) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that all markers are installed and remain in place, and that the 
area is growing back.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to June 17, 2027.  Seconded 
by Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.
Page 6 
 
Q.  Enforcement Order #25-006 – 2 Muirfield Lane – Aniberquiz Baez (Continued from August 
20, 2026) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the property owner is in total compliance.  The fill had 
been moved, the area had been revegetated, and the arborvitaes had been moved. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to June 17, 2027. Seconded by 
Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
R.  Notice of Violation #26-002 – 2 Indian Summer Street – Galloway (Continued from August 
20, 2026) 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the site is in compliance and recommended continuation 
to late summer.  
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to August 19, 2027. Seconded 
by Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
S.  Notice of Violation #26-006 – 143B Tyler Street – Aaron DiGloria (Continued from August 
20, 2026)  
 
The Conservation Officer reported that the property owner was working with Merrimack 
Engineering to prepare a wetland plan, violation plan, and restoration plan.  The Conservation 
Officer stated that the proposed project that triggered the matter likely would not start until the 
site is brought into compliance.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to November 19, 2026. 
Seconded by Rachel Letcher.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
T.  Public Hearing vs.  Public Meeting – Discussion/Review 
 
The Commission discussed a draft policy addressing public hearings, public meetings, and a 
three-minute rule for public comment.  Kenneth Sateriale stated that the revised draft 
incorporated Patrice Friant’s recommendation to expand the discretion of the Chair. 
The Commission discussed that the Chair would announce the three-minute limit, that the Chair 
would have discretion to allow additional time when necessary, and that the limit would not 
apply to applicants or their representatives.  The Commission also discussed that comments must 
only address issues within the purview of the Commission.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Kenneth Sateriale to adopt the document as a policy of the 
Commission.  Seconded by Rachel Lecher.  Aye: Friant, Lecher, and Sateriale; Nay: Boulay and 
Di Zazzo.  Vote: Approved, 3-2.  
 
U.  Emergency Certification – 296 Hampshire Road – DPW Beaver Dam Breach 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that a beaver dam was breached by DPW because a nearby 
house was close to the brook and the City was preparing for an impending storm.  The 
Conservation Officer stated that the purpose was to be proactive because the residence was close 
to the brook and occupied by an elderly couple.
Page 7 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to ratify the Emergency Certification.  Seconded by 
Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
9. CONSERVATION OFFICER’S REPORT 
A.  Rabies Exposure – Conservation Officer Christopher Parsons 
 
The agenda stated that Conservation Officer Christopher Parsons was exposed to rabies while 
responding to a call from a concerned resident regarding an animal, that the animal was 
euthanized and submitted for rabies testing, that the test result was negative, and that Officer 
Parsons received rabies vaccinations as a precaution while awaiting results.  
The Conservation Officer reported that the animal was an injured skunk, that the animal was sent 
to Bulger Animal Hospital for testing, and that the testing invoice was approximately $193.00.  
The Commission discussed the matter and the assistance previously provided by Bulger Animal 
Hospital.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Kenneth Sateriale to release Commission funds to pay the animal 
testing expense, in the amount of approximately $193.00.  Seconded by Sandra Boulay.  All in 
favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
B.  Rental Truck – Conservation Records 
 
The Office of Community Development requested authorization to release Commission funds to 
cover the cost of a rental truck needed to move Conservation Commission records from the 
Pleasant Valley School to the Searles Estate, with the final cost based on the length of the rental 
and anticipated to be approximately $400.00 or less.  
The Conservation Officer reported that Conservation records stored at the Pleasant Valley 
School must be moved and maintained.  The records include file cabinets that must remain in 
numerical order.  
The Conservation Officer stated that DPW needed a rack-body truck with an electric tailgate to 
move the cabinets and that the Commission and the Office of Community Development would 
split the rental cost.  The maximum Conservation share was estimated not to exceed $400.00. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to release funds for the records move, not to exceed 
$400.00.  Seconded by Rachel Letcher.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
C. Liam’s Lane – Tree Removal / Conservation Area 
 
The Conservation Officer reported that a resident contacted the office and the Mayor’s Office 
regarding a tree within a conservation easement near Liam’s Lane.  The Conservation Officer 
inspected the area and explained that the property line was close to the side of the house.  
The Conservation Officer stated that, although it was unclear whether the tree was on the 
resident’s property or conservation property, the tree was definitely within the conservation 
easement under the jurisdiction of the Commission.  The Conservation Officer offered to issue 
an emergency certification that would allow the tree to be reduced in height and branched out, 
with material handled consistently with Commission policy.  The resident declined that offer and 
requested full removal of the tree.  
The Director of Community Development informed the Commission that the Mayor instructed 
the City Solicitor to prepare a waiver authorizing the property owner to remove the entire tree, 
without requiring the tree to be reduced in height or branched out, and providing a waiver of
Page 8 
liability.  The Commission expressed concern regarding the procedure followed and decided to 
send a letter to the City Solicitor to address the matter and clarify the proper protocol for matters 
within the jurisdiction of the Conservation Commission. 
MOTION: Motion made by Kenneth Sateriale to send the letter. Seconded by Patrice Friant.  All 
in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
10. OTHER BUSINESS 
A. 397 Transmission Line – DEP File #219-1321, MCC File #26-002 – Request for Reissue of 
Order of Conditions 
 
The Commission discussed a request to reissue the Order of Conditions for the 397 Transmission 
Line project.  The Conservation Officer explained that the Order of Conditions had already been 
issued, but certain wording needed to be revised. 
The Conservation Officer stated that language regarding a bond was removed because the bond 
had previously been waived.  References to the project being performed in phases were also 
removed because any new work would require a new Notice of Intent.  The Conservation Officer 
stated that the other recommendations remained, including matting-related conditions.  
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to reissue the Order of Conditions. Seconded by 
Rachel Letcher.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
  
11. ADJOURNMENT 
There being no further business, a motion to adjourn was made by Patrice Friant and 
seconded by Rachel Lecher.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  The meeting adjourned at 
approximately 8:04 PM.  
Respectfully submitted by, 
Dave Di Zazzo 
 
Approved by: 
Kenneth Sateriale, Secretary 
 
 
Submitted for the Commission: 
Michelle Davidson, Clerk 
 
 
 
Date:
